ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (15) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form).

This is Tolstoy's Russian version of the Declaration of Sentiments of the Boston Peace Convention (1838), translated from his wording, not restored to Garrison's English: «кафтан» (kaftan, 'caftan') stays in the Matthew 5:40 allusion, and «возрождение» (vozrozhdenie, 'regeneration'), «человечество» (chelovechestvo, 'mankind'), and «непротивление злу злом» (neprotivlenie zlu zlom, 'non-resistance to evil by evil') are held constant. The source's lowercase «царь царствующих и господь господствующих» (tsar' tsarstvuyushchikh i gospod' gospodstvuyushchikh) is 'the king of kings and Lord of lords', with «господь» capitalized as 'Lord' by the book's rule.

Source observation: [5] «признаем нехристианским незаконным» (priznaem nekhristianskim nezakonnym, 'we recognize as unchristian unlawful') lacks the «и» ('and') printed in the parallel phrases before and after it; translated as 'unchristian and unlawful'.
